statement: Define ValidBST(t) for every finite Tree t by: ValidBST(Null) is true; ValidBST(Node(v,L,R)) is true exactly when ValidBST(L) and ValidBST(R), every key occurring in L is < v, and every key occurring in R is > v. The function returns a result r : Bool (it does not fail), and r = true if and only if ValidBST(root) is true; equivalently, r = false if and only if ValidBST(root) is false.
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]. In particular root is not Null.

statement: The call is_valid_bst root returns a result (an Ok Bool value) rather than failing.
preconditions: None beyond root being a finite Tree; root may be Null, may have any number of Node occurrences, and keys may be any i64 values.

statement: Whenever the function returns true, for every node occurrence u with key v, every node occurrence in the left subtree of u has key < v, and every node occurrence in the right subtree of u has key > v. Here the left subtree of u is the entire tree rooted at u's left child, including all descendants; if u has no such child the condition is vacuous.
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]. In particular root is not Null.

statement: Whenever the function returns false, there exist two distinct node occurrences u and v such that either v lies in the left subtree of u and key(v) >= key(u), or v lies in the right subtree of u and key(v) <= key(u).
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]. In particular root is not Null.

statement: If there are two distinct node occurrences in root with equal keys, then the function returns false.
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]. In particular root is not Null.

statement: Whenever the function returns true, the in-order traversal of root is strictly increasing. The in-order traversal is the sequence formed by recursively listing the left subtree, then the node key, then the right subtree, with Null contributing no elements; strictly increasing means for every index i with 0 <= i < len(sequence) - 1, sequence[i] < sequence[i+1].
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]. In particular root is not Null.

statement: Whenever the function returns true, for every node occurrence u with key v: if the left subtree of u is nonempty, then the maximum key among all node occurrences in that left subtree is < v; if the right subtree of u is nonempty, then the minimum key among all node occurrences in that right subtree is > v.
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]. In particular root is not Null.

statement: Whenever the function returns true, for every node occurrence u, every key in the left subtree of u is strictly less than every key in the right subtree of u. If either subtree is empty, this condition is vacuous.
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]. In particular root is not Null.

statement: Define mirror_neg(root) recursively by mirror_neg(Null) = Null and mirror_neg(Node(v,L,R)) = Node(-v, mirror_neg(R), mirror_neg(L)). The function returns a Bool for root and for mirror_neg(root), and these two Bool results are equal.
preconditions: root is a finite Tree whose keys are all in [-2147483648, 2147483647].

statement: Let shift_c(root) be the tree with the same shape as root in which every node key v is replaced by v + c. The function returns Ok r for root and Ok r' for shift_c(root) (it does not fail), and r = r'.
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]; c is an integer such that for every key v occurring in root, v + c is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647].

statement: The function returns Ok r (it does not fail), and r = true if and only if the in-order traversal of root is strictly increasing. The in-order traversal and strict increase are as defined in spec_6: recursively list the left subtree, then the node key, then the right subtree, with Null contributing no elements; strictly increasing means every adjacent pair in the sequence satisfies sequence[i] < sequence[i+1].
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]. In particular root is not Null.

statement: If there exist two distinct node occurrences u and v such that either v lies in the left subtree of u and key(v) >= key(u), or v lies in the right subtree of u and key(v) <= key(u), then the function returns false (and does not fail). Equivalently, together with spec_4, the function returns false if and only if such a violating ancestor-descendant pair exists.
preconditions: root is a finite Tree with 1 <= number of Node occurrences <= 10000; every node key is an integer in [-2147483648, 2147483647]. In particular root is not Null.
